summary: Orphaned stream tail after mobile network handover causes missing final paragraph and duplicate punctuation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when their mobile app (iOS/Android) experiences a cellular->WiFi handover during a streaming response, the final paragraph of the generated response is missing; the last visible chunk sometimes contains duplicated terminal punctuation (e.g., '... end of sentence..'). This appears on both SSE and WebSocket-backed streams.

Impact:
- A single dedicated-customer (Noteable Analytics) is seeing truncated explanations in customer-facing report generation flows.
- Affects short and long responses; higher chance on >6s streaming sessions and when client resumes over a new network path.

Environment:
- Production (dedicated capacity) in us-east-1
- Customer using Redwood SDK v0.9.8 (JS mobile embed) with SDK streaming enabled (SSE preferred, WS fallback).
- Edge layer: internal edge-proxy cluster + Cloud Provider LB + client NAT/CGNAT on mobile.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Start a streaming request (SSE) from mobile on cellular with a ~10s generation expected.
2) Trigger a network handover (toggle airplane mode or move into WiFi coverage).
3) Client SDK reconnects and resumes stream.
4) Observe final paragraph missing or trailing punctuation duplicated.

Observed behavior:
- Final paragraph not present in assembled output (server-side logs show last chunk emitted but client-side stream stops before finalization).
- When stream does reach a terminal choice, the final token often duplicates punctuation or has short repetition.
- Resume events in logs show a short gap and an edge-proxy connection handoff at the same time.

Expected behavior:
- Stream resumes without losing terminal chunks; final paragraph and punctuation intact and idempotent.

Attachments/Logs: see 'logs' field for extracted excerpts and a link to the customer's sample session on S3 (redacted).

comments: 2026-03-10 15:22 — Support (Aisha Patel): Logged initial ticket after customer chat. Captured sample session and SDK debug logs (attached to ticket). Asked customer to try WS mode and to capture a pcap if possible.

2026-03-10 16:05 — Customer (Laura G, Noteable): We reproduced reliably when moving between networks in our lab. WS had similar symptoms. We've attached full SDK debug output and a short screen recording.

2026-03-10 18:12 — SRE (Sanjay Iyer): Edge logs show a connection handoff and a FIN before client ACK in several sessions. Hypothesis: client-side half-close during NAT rebind causes proxy to flush and not forward final terminal chunk before TCP teardown. Investigating whether resume ACK path is reliably replaying final frame.

2026-03-11 09:34 — Engineer (Marco Ruiz): Reproduced locally using simulated path migration. Observed the serving runtime emitted final chunk but edge-proxy's write buffer saw an ECONNRESET before the client's SSE handler processed it. Added additional logging to capture edge write attempts and socket states.

2026-03-11 13:00 — Support (Aisha Patel): Provided customer with a temporary client-side mitigation: enable 'graceful-reconnect' heuristic in SDK (v0.9.9-beta) which introduces a 200ms pre-resume ACK window and retries the last delta fetch. Customer asked for a patch that doesn't require altering their production app.
2026-03-12 11:48 — Engineer (Marco Ruiz): Opened PR to edge-proxy to treat late FINs as write failures with retry buffer (PR #2890). Running canary in staging with simulated NAT rebinding.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge-proxy flush+teardown race — on network handoff the client socket is half-closed; edge proxy attempts to write final chunk but TCP RST/FIN races and kernel drops payload before it reaches client user-space handler.

Hypothesis 2: Resume offset mismatch — client resume requests offset one less than server's last emitted seq; server treats it as duplicate and suppresses re-sending final token (less likely; checks show offsets match in sample).
Repro steps for engineering: use 'tc' to simulate path migrate; reproduce with both SSE and WS layers; monitor kernel socket states and write syscall return codes on edge-proxy host.

Preliminary finding: write syscall returns EPIPE on edge-proxy in ~36% of repro runs; serving-runtime still marks 'final=true' as emitted. Client-level SDK often discards incomplete frames if underlying socket reset occurs before userland parse triggers.
resolution: Mitigation provided: support shared SDK patch (v0.9.9-beta) with a configurable pre-resume grace window and idempotent last-chunk fetch. Engineering has an edge-proxy change (PR #2890) to add a short retransmit buffer and treat EPIPE as retriable for the final chunk. Canary tests show elimination of truncation in staging with simulated NAT rebinding. Customer requested scheduled rollout to their dedicated cluster after 48h canary. Permanent fix: edge-proxy change merged pending full CI + rollout.
root_cause: Race between edge-proxy connection teardown on client path migration and final-chunk propagation; client SDK does not always recover the final terminal frame when TCP-level reset occurs before user-space SSE handler processes the buffer.
suggested_next_steps: 1) Complete edge-proxy PR review and merge; 2) Promote SDK patch to GA and coordinate customer upgrade; 3) Add an edge-level metric for 'final-chunk-retransmit' and an alert for >1% in production; 4) Update streaming runbook with mobile handover guidance and recommended SDK flags.
public_notes: Customer-facing summary: We identified a network handover race that can cause the final paragraph of a streamed response to be lost. A temporary SDK patch and an upcoming edge-proxy update are being rolled out; we will coordinate a scheduled upgrade for your dedicated cluster and provide follow-up validation steps.
internal_priority_notes: P1 due to customer impact on production dedicated cluster; mitigation reduces customer-visible errors but full rollout required. Monitor canary and set pager threshold if retransmit metric exceeds 0.5%.
